name: Avartack the Champion

facts.text: Level 65, 30,000 health, a realm-raid final. He fights with crushing blows and casts Avartack's Force, 300 body damage.
He cannot be hurt outside his tether.
'Avartack' is unglossed; the champion's oath is Living Server lore.

story:
Every chieftain had a champion, the man who stood in the ford so his lord need not, and Avartack was Caimheul's. He swore the champion's oath: to stand before his lord until his lord no longer needed him. Caimheul died. The oath did not say what to do then, so Avartack was buried at his lord's feet, and when the keeners sang them both back he simply took up his post again. He fights like a man defending a ford, heavy and unmoving, and when he lays a hand on his enemy the force of it goes straight through armour into the body. He does not leave his floor. He never left the ford either.

In the old hill wars two war-bands would meet at a ford, and before the slaughter each chieftain would send his champion into the water to fight the other's. If your champion won, sometimes there was no slaughter at all. Avartack was Caimheul's champion for twenty years and never lost at the ford, and the keeners' daughters say Caimheul's people were spared more battles by that one man than by all the chieftain's hardness together.

His oath was the champion's oath: to stand before his lord until his lord no longer needed him. Nobody told him when that was. He was buried at his lord's feet, and when the keeners sang them both back he took his post again before the chieftain's hall, on a floor he still thinks of as a ford. He fights heavy and unmoving, with crushing blows, and when he lays his hand on an enemy a force goes out of him that passes through armour into the body. He cannot be drawn from his floor: beyond it no blow lands on him. The Blue Lady sang for the blades he broke at the ford, and some of them rise in her room still.
legend: A straight fight, but a hard one: his force spell goes through armour, so the healers watch the cloth classes. He will not be pulled off his floor; fight him there. Clear the living dead around him before you start. Clear the floor around him first and fight him on it. His force spell is the danger: cloth and leather classes stay out of his reach and the healers watch them. Superstition in the hill country: salute him before the pull, champion to champion. The tanks who do it swear he fights them cleaner. Nobody can prove otherwise, and nobody wants to be the one who stopped saluting.

aggro: No one passes. My lord is resting.
The ford is mine. Turn back.
Twenty years, and no one crossed.

loremasterTopic.text: Caimheul's champion, who swore to stand before his lord until he was no longer needed. Nobody told him when that was.

bookPage: From Nóra's book: my grandmother's grandmother saw Avartack fight at the ford of the Erne, or said she did. She said he was not tall, but that when he stepped into the water the other war-band's champion stepped back out of it, and the two chieftains went home without a battle. That was the best of the old hill wars, she said: the champion took the death so the rest did not. He is still taking it, under Breifine, on a floor he thinks is the river. When the realm's raid ends his watch, someone should tell him the ford is held. He would like to know.
